nodes.quote: On the other hand, F2 is the most stable fault, because it has the lowest $T _ { \mathrm { s } }$ and $T _ { \mathrm { s m } }$ and can undergo an average maximum pore pressure of 55–57 MPa.

Results of all three methods of 3D Mohr diagrams, slip tendency and modifed slip tendency, confrmed that F2 is the most stable fault in the feld, and it can sustain a maximum pore pressure of 55–57 MPa.
Results demonstrated that both equations are in accordance with each other.

For this purpose, by using the equation derived in the NISOC laboratory, static elastic moduli were calculated to estimate the current stress regime of the feld, and then the accuracy of the results was examined by the Seyed Sajadi and Aghighi (2015) equation.
10 shows, none of the faults is critically stressed in the current stress feld.

A total number of 32 fractures were observed in the studied well, with a prevailing azimuth of $5 2 ^ { \circ }$ (the existence of drillinginduced tensile fractures is $9 0 ^ { \circ }$ from the breakouts).

nodes.quote: 13 shows, all the faults are inactive at the present stress state, and the estimated horizontal stresses fall within the normal faulting triangle (triangle with solid lines).
By increasing pore pressure to its critical value, horizontal stresses will be positioned on the left edge of the smaller
triangle (triangle with dashed lines) showing the risk of reactivation.

8, in this feld the maximum principal stress $( \sigma _ { 1 } )$ is $\sigma _ { \mathrm { V } } ,$ and the intermediate and minimum principal stresses $( \sigma _ { 2 }$ and $\sigma _ { 3 } )$ are $\sigma _ { \mathrm { H m a x } }$ and $\sigma _ { \mathrm { h m i n } } ,$ respectively.
${ \mathrm { S o } } ,$ according to Anderson’s faulting theory (Anderson 1951), this feld is in a normal faulting regime (i.e., $\sigma _ { 1 } { > } \sigma _ { 2 } { > } \sigma _ { 3 } )$ .

Fig. 13 Stress polygons plotted for the four faults. Three triangles NF, SS, and RF represent the normal, strike-slip and reverse faulting regimes, respectively. The blue solid lines represent the current stress feld and pore pressure. Black dashed lines represent the stress feld in critical pore pressure obtained by 3D Mohr diagrams. Circle and diamond shaped points represent the NISOC and Seyed Sajadi and Aghighi (2015) equations for obtaining elastic moduli used for estimating the horizontal stresses magnitudes

Fig. 8 Stress-depth plots showing the stress state in the Gachsaran oilfeld (with the line of best ft) (left), and a well faulted by F2 (right). The gray points represent the formation fuid pressures (RFT), and triangles indicate FIT pressure (the stresses are calculated using the elastic moduli estimated by the NISOC equation)

Fig. 10 3D Mohr diagrams of four faults F1, F2, F3, and F4 (using the NISOC equation). As can be seen, none of the faults is critically stressed, and all of them are stable in the current stress feld and pore pressure
